parole.significato: alaudid (member of the Alaudidae taxonomic genus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Alaudidae, derived from Latin alauda, borrowed from Gaulish *alauda (“skylark”).

parole.significato: vole, field mouse
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Arvicola, derived from Latin arvum (“field”) + -cola (suffix indicating an inhabitant).

parole.significato: any plant of the Batrachium taxonomic subgenus of genus Ranunculus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Batrachium, from Latin batrachium, batrachion, from Ancient Greek βατράχιον (batrákhion), diminutive of βάτραχος (bátrakhos, “frog”).

parole.significato: bombax (plant of the Bombax genus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Bombax, from Medieval Latin bombax, alternative form of bambax (“cotton wool”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Bulbocodium taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Bulbocodium, derived from Latin bulbus (“bulb”) + Ancient Greek κῴδιον (kōídion, “sheepskin”).

parole.significato: any plant in the Cacalia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Cacalia, from Latin cacālia, from Ancient Greek κακκαλίᾱ (kakkalíā).

parole.significato: kalanchoe
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Kalanchoe, from New Latin Kalanchauhuy as recorded by Georg Joseph Kamel, from a Sinitic source akin to Cantonese 伽藍菜 /伽蓝菜 (gaa¹ laam⁴ coi³, literally “temple plant”).

parole.significato: calla (Calla palustris)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Calla, from Latin calla.

parole.significato: any member of the Caniformia taxonomic suborder
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Caniformia, from Latin canifōrmis (“dog-shaped”).

parole.significato: any member of the family Cassididae, a synonym of the Cassidae
parole.testo: From translingual Cassididae, derived from Cassis, from Latin cassis (“metal helmet”).

parole.significato: any of the plants of the genus Costus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Costus, from Latin costus.

parole.significato: any wrasse of the Symphodus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Crenilabrus, derived from Latin crēna (“incision, notch”) + labrum (“lip”).

parole.significato: difflugid
parole.testo: From translingual Difflugia, derived from Latin diffluō.

parole.significato: any member of the Dracaena taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Dracaena, from Late Latin dracaena, from Ancient Greek δράκαινα (drákaina, “she-dragon”). Doublet of tracina.

parole.significato: rupturewort, burstwort (of genus Herniaria)
parole.testo: From translingual Herniaria, from Latin hernia.

parole.significato: synonym of mochi (“bitter vetch”)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Ervum, from Latin ervum (“vetch”).

parole.significato: any member of the Phallus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Phallus, from Latin phallus, from Ancient Greek φαλλός (phallós, “penis”).

parole.significato: any fungus of the genus Fusicladium.
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Fusicladium, derived from Latin fūsus + Ancient Greek κλάδιον (kládion), diminutive of κλάδος (kládos, “branch”).

parole.significato: any member of the Gobiidae taxonomic family of gobies
parole.testo: From translingual Gobiidae, from the name of the genus Gobius, from Latin gōbius (“gudgeon”).

parole.significato: the Lactarius genus of mushrooms
parole.testo: From translingual Lactarius, from Latin lactārius (“pertaining to milk”).

parole.significato: honey badger (Mellivora)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Mellivora, derived from Latin mellem (“honey”) + -vorus (“-eating, -devouring”, adjectival suffix).

parole.significato: bee-eater
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Merops, from Latin merops, from Ancient Greek μέροψ (mérops).

parole.significato: any member of the Mugilidae taxonomic family
parole.testo: From translingual Mugilidae, derived from Latin mūgil (“mullet”) + -idus (“tending to”).

parole.significato: any member of the Mugiliformes taxonomic order
parole.testo: From translingual Mugiliformes, derived from Latin mūgil (“mullet”) + -fōrmis (“-shaped”).

parole.significato: black-crowned night heron (Nycticorax nycticorax)
parole.testo: From translingual Nycticorax, from Latin nycticorax, from Ancient Greek νυκτικόραξ (nuktikórax, literally “night crow”).

parole.significato: any lichen of the taxonomic genus Parmelia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Parmelia, derived from Latin parma (“shield”).

parole.significato: purslane (any plant of the family Portulacaceae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Portulaca, from Latin portulāca. Doublet of porcacchia.

parole.significato: any plant of the Potamogeton taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Potamogeton, from Latin potamogēton, from Ancient Greek ποταμογείτων (potamogeítōn).

parole.significato: any rodent of the Proechimys taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Proechimys, derived from Latin prō- + Ancient Greek ἐχῖνος (ekhînos, “hedgehog”) + μῦς (mûs, “mouse, rat”).

parole.significato: any of the genus Serrasalmus of piranhas
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Serrasalmus, derived from Latin serra (“saw”) + salmō (“salmon”).

parole.significato: any member of the Sparidae taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Sparidae, derived from Latin sparus (“spear, javelin”).

parole.significato: any member of the Squalidae taxonomic family
parole.testo: From translingual Squalidae, from the name of the genus Squalus, from Latin squālus.

parole.significato: any plant in the Terminalia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Terminalia, from Late Latin terminālis.

parole.significato: tridacna (clam of the genus Tridacna)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Tridacna, from the neuter plural Latin tridacna, from Ancient Greek τρίδακνος (trídaknos), derived from τρι- (tri-, “three”) + δάκνω (dáknō, “to bite”).

parole.significato: veratrum, white hellebore (Veratrum album)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Veratrum, from Latin vērātrum (“hellebore”).

parole.significato: a member of the Zea taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Zea, from Latin zēa (“spelt”), from Ancient Greek ζειά (zeiá).
